newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-GOUGH LEADS ENGLAND TO INNINGS VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GOUGH LEADS ENGLAND TO INNINGS VICTORY.

text.p: England, led by paceman Darren Gough, turned around their tour of Zimbabwe and New Zealand on Monday by comprehensively beating New Zealand by an innings and 68 runs.
England go one up in the three match series after the first test was drawn.
Gough ripped through New Zealand, who resumed at 125 for four, in a withering morning session and finished with figures of four for 52 to go with his first innings haul of five for 40.
The win gave a loyal group of England supporters known as the "Barmy Army" something to cheer about after a long wait.
For Mike Atherton, the victory will be a welcome tonic as he and his team answered their army of critics in the best possible way.
They were lambasted for losing the one-day series on the first leg of the tour in Zimbabwe and only managing a drawn test series.
Then, in the first test in Auckland England allowed New Zealand to escape with a draw, thanks to a record last-wicket stand lasting over three hours by Danny Morrison and Nathan Astle.
Worse followed, with a loss to New Zealand A between the two tests.
Atherton singled out fast bowlers Gough and New Zealand-raised Andrew Caddick for exceptional bowling.

"I think throughout the winter, I know you talk about a difficult time in Zimbabwe, but in the longer form of the game we played good cricket there as well and dominated the first test match there as well," Atherton told a Television New Zealand reporter after the match.
"I've been really happy how the side is playing test match cricket, and I think although we haven't won all the games, if your level of performance is good, sooner or later you'll start winning."
England team members almost outmatched the Barmy Army in their celebrations, singing and spraying each other with champagne.
On Monday England showed there was to be no escape for New Zealand at the Basin Reserve. Rain, which delayed the resumption by half an hour, was New Zealand's main hope.
Requiring 259 to make England bat a second time, only opener Blair Pocock showed any real resistance.
Bowling into the brisk wind, Gough sliced through the middle order before lunch.
He had captain Lee Germon play onto his stumps to his fourth ball of the day, then had the stubborn Pocock brilliantly caught at second slip by Nick Knight for 64 in his next over.

First test century-maker Nathan Astle's uncomfortable stay was ended by a superb diving catch by wicketkeeper Alec Stewart and three balls later Simon Doull's awful push at a ball outside his off stump gave Knight his second catch of the innings.
After Pocock and Germon's diligent fifth-wicket stand of 36 was been broken, there was little further resistance.
Pocock batted 338 minutes, faced 270 balls and hit five fours in a defiant performance.
Gough received excellent support from seamer Caddick, who bowled beautifully, finishing off the innings after lunch when he bowled Geoff Allott and had Chris Cairns caught by Knight at second slip.

While Atherton may now be able to relax a little, the heat may now go on Germon and the New Zealanders who have been criticised for partying into the early hours of the morning during this test and for their dismal batting displays.
